question: In which language was Heart Lamp originally written?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kannada**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• The book **“Heart Lamp”** was originally written in the **Kannada language**, which is one of the **Dravidian languages** spoken predominantly in the Indian state of **Karnataka**. 
• **Kannada** is recognized as one of the **scheduled languages** in the Constitution of India and has a rich literary tradition that dates back over a thousand years. 
• The original author of "Heart Lamp" has contributed significantly to Kannada literature, which often explores themes of **philosophy, spirituality, and culture**. 
• Karnataka, the home of the Kannada language, is known for its **vibrant literary history**, with many renowned authors and poets contributing to its diverse literary heritage. 
• It is important to note that Kannada literature has been honored with **Jnanpith Awards**, which is India’s highest literary honor. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Kannada Language:** 
• **Kannada** is a Dravidian language primarily spoken by over **44 million people** in Karnataka and neighboring states such as Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, and Maharashtra. 
• The language has a **distinct script** that evolved from the ancient Brahmi script. Kannada is known for its **complex grammar** and rich vocabulary. 
• Kannada literature is classified into three broad periods: **Old Kannada (450–1200 CE)**, **Middle Kannada (1200–1700 CE)**, and **Modern Kannada (1700 CE–present).** 
• **Literary Significance of Kannada:** 
• Karnataka has produced **eight Jnanpith Award winners**, including iconic writers like Kuvempu and Girish Karnad, reflecting the richness of Kannada literature. 
• Many Kannada works have been translated into other Indian and international languages, showcasing the **universal appeal** of its literary themes. 
• **Alternative Languages in the Options:** 
• **Tamil:** Another Dravidian language with a long history, primarily spoken in Tamil Nadu and Sri Lanka. It is unrelated to "Heart Lamp." 
• **Hindi:** An Indo-Aryan language predominantly spoken in northern and central India. While popular, it is not the language of origin for "Heart Lamp." 
• **Malayalam:** A language spoken in Kerala and parts of Lakshadweep, also part of the Dravidian family, but unrelated to this work. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Kannada's Classical Language Status:** Kannada was awarded the status of a **Classical Language** of India in 2008 due to its long-standing literary tradition and rich history. 
• **Global Reach:** Kannada-speaking communities are found worldwide, with literature and cultural programs promoting the language globally. 
• **Prominent Works:** Apart from “Heart Lamp,” Kannada literature includes notable works like “Ramayana Darshanam” by Kuvempu and “Samskara” by U.R. Ananthamurthy.
